title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Telex Release
content:
A telex release is the `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` service by which the consignee collects the cargo at destination without producing any original, because the shipper has already given the originals up at the port of origin. This page states who may ask for it, what makes it effective, how it is recorded and how it is charged.

## Clauses

1. **Availability.** The service exists only for document types that offer a telex release.
2. **Who may ask.** A telex release, a correction and a switch bill may each be requested only by the documentation party that holds the document record. The holder is identified from the customer named on the document record.
3. **Pending with the shipper.** A telex release request is registered on the document and remains pending with the shipper, since handing in the originals is something only the shipper can do.
4. **When it takes effect.** A telex release takes effect when the full set of originals has been handed in at the origin office, leaving nothing outstanding on the document.
5. **Recording.** The documentation history shows the hand-in as a surrender, at the origin office, of the originals of the set in force; the document then carries the status surrendered. Release of the cargo at destination is then dealt with under the rules on destination release.
6. **Charge.** A telex release is charged the type's telex release fee, payable by the documentation party.
7. **Status for the charge.** The telex release fee can be entered only against a document whose status is surrendered.
8. **Once per request.** A release request is never charged more than once.
9. **Irrevocable.** After the document has become surrendered, the telex release cannot be withdrawn.

## Retired exemption

Under an earlier wording of clause 6, the fee was not charged where the documentation party itself held an active service contract whose tier rank reached the type's exemption threshold, a zero threshold meaning that no contract exempted the fee. That exemption test is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current contract-based exemption for the telex release fee, which rests on a different contract test; the retired test must not be applied.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Situation on record | Result |
|---|---|
| Caller is not the documentation party of the document | May not request the telex release |
| Request registered, originals still with the shipper | Request pending; no release yet |
| Full set handed in at origin | Document surrendered; release effective |
| Document surrendered, customer wishes to cancel the telex release | Not possible |

## Basis Q&A

**Can the consignee ask for the telex release?** Only if the consignee is itself the documentation party holding the record.

**Does a telex release by itself put the cargo in the consignee's hands?** It makes the release effective; delivery at destination then follows the destination release rules, on the strength of the surrendered document.

superseded_clauses: except when the documentation party holds an active service contract whose tier rank is at least the tier's telex_fee_waiver_min_contract_rank, a value of 0 meaning that no contract exempts the fee.
